title: kv-cache: adaptive defrag + spillover eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and reactive paging/spillover cause unexpected latency spikes under tail workloads and mixed sequence-length traffic. This PR introduces an adaptive defragmentation and spillover eviction policy that works with the existing paging layer to reduce page churn and maintain latency SLOs.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Implements cooperative background defragmentation that is triggered by a new fragmentation metric (fragmentation_ratio) computed per KV shard. Adds a hysteresis-aware spillover eviction policy: when memory pressure is detected the policy preferentially spills low-reuse entries and applies chunk-aligned eviction to prevent creating many small free fragments. Integrates with the scheduler so defrag/backfill work is scheduled as low-priority background tasks that yield to inference work and respect per-GPU throughput SLOs. Improves memory accounting: track allocation buckets and introduce compacted-chunk descriptors to allow O(1) coalescing when free ranges are adjacent. Adds unit and integration tests and a benchmark harness to reproduce mixed-length tail scenarios. The description below includes checklist and links.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc referenced: Linear ENG-6421 (internal design)
- [x] New fragmentation metric and telemetry
- [x] Background defrag worker with cooperative yielding
- [x] Spillover eviction that prefers low-reuse / chunk-aligned eviction
- [x] Scheduler integration and rate-limiting for background work
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks + perf results added to PR comment

See related PRs: pr-41234-kv-cache-eviction-spillover-heuristics.json, pr-35821-kv-cache-memory-eviction-spillover-optimizations.json.

benchmarks_summary: Tail-workload benchmark: 95th p99 latency reduced from 183ms -> 124ms on n1-standard-equivalent test harness; paging events reduced by ~67%; overall token throughput stable within 2%. Bench harness attached as perf/kv_cache_tail_workload.py
review_comments: Marco Li: Can you explain how fragmentation_ratio is computed and whether it adds measurable CPU overhead?

Aisha Patel: fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_chunk / total_free_bytes) per shard; computed incrementally on frees/allocs, cost amortized and only sampled for telemetry every 10s. Measured <0.2% cpu overhead in stress tests.
Renee Thompson: Background defrag sounds dangerous if it competes with inference. How is scheduling handled?

Aisha Patel: defrag work is registered as a low-priority task with the scheduler; it yields after processing N chunks or if measured tail latency exceeds configured threshold. Added unit tests to assert yielding behavior.
Diego Alvarez: What about compatibility with existing spillover to host? Any races during coalesce?

Aisha Patel: Added per-shard mutex for allocator metadata; page-backed spillover remains atomic. Coalesce only touches chunk descriptors; we validate under TSAN in integration tests. See tests/kv_cache/test_defrag_integration.cpp for race coverage.
Marco Li: Request small API comment clarifications and one nits on variable names in allocator.cpp
Aisha Patel: Addressed nits in follow-up commit b3e2fa1. Marking as resolved.
requested_changes: Initial review requested to add more telemetry tags to correlate fragmentation spikes with model and sequence-length distributions (requested by Renee).
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive defragmentation and chunk-aligned spillover eviction reduce paging and tail latency. Backwards compatible. Recommended to enable by default in Dedicated private deployments after monitoring for 1 week.
notes_for_ops: Telemetry: new metrics kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache.defrag_cycles, kv_cache.spill_events. Add alert if fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 for 5m across >50% shards. Default defrag worker is enabled but rate-limited; config knobs available in runtime.conf: kv_cache.defrag.enabled, kv_cache.defrag.max_chunks_per_cycle, kv_cache.eviction.chunk_alignment_bytes.
perf_regression_check: none detected; microbench shows improvement for mixed-length workloads; CI perf canary green
